AI models and governed digital workers

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Explain model provenance
  • Trace kill-switch enforcement
  • Describe proposal-only workers

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Approved installation
  2. 02Model + prompt
  3. 03Input minimization
  4. 04Dual guardrails
  5. 05Proposal
  6. 06Human approval
  7. 07Mutation + lineage

1. Models do not become policy

Model output enters as a provenance-tagged fact with model/version/use-case lineage.

Material influence invokes human review.

Deterministic rules — not a model response — own the final executable outcome.

2. Kill switch

Model governance owns global, model and workflow switch state; the decision engine enforces it. A disabled or unvalidated dependency degrades model-dependent work to manual review.

3. Workers

Marketplace installations require commercial, role, staffing and guardrail activation.

Workers propose CAM, underwriting, document or service outputs; independent humans approve material actions.

Execution retains installation, model, prompt, guardrail, input and output lineage.
